stem:
A rope is $12.6\ \mathrm{m}$ long. Vimal cuts it into pieces of $0.9\ \mathrm{m}$ each.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Ignore the piece length $0.9\ \mathrm{m}$ and report $12.6$ as the number of pieces.
The same count also covers every rope length, not only $12.6\ \mathrm{m}$ with $0.9\ \mathrm{m}$ pieces.
Read only the digit $6$ in $12.6$ to decide the number of pieces.

teacher.key_rationale: In common units of metres, the number of pieces is the quotient 12.6÷0.9=14. Omitting the piece length, widening the claim to every rope, or reading only the digit 6 all miss that hinge.
